steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 49.43 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the flat side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 0° (blade upright). Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, left of the blade, is a square-ended block 0.50 in long. This cut meets the side of the next ring piece.

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the flat side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Measure from the first cut and mark: 48.68 in along the point; 48.68 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the flat side; 48.68 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the sawn face that lies on the flat side -- the blade follows that line. steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as ring 1, long side: on a sawn face against the flat side, point toward the open run (like the frame).

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).

Lay the rings from the frame inward. Each ring is a small frame: three pieces in the same pinwheel as the frame -- each runs from the far side of the piece behind it to the near side of the piece ahead, square-cut both ends in plan.
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
Centre: a triangle 8.6 in across its inscribed circle is left. Fill it with a plug cut from one wedge laid flat, or leave it open as a vent.
fitting: The first piece meets the 45° slope with its bark: it touches along one line, and leaves a wedge-shaped gap above it -- caulk it or pack it.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).

Lay the rings from the frame inward. Each ring is a small frame: three pieces in the same pinwheel as the frame -- each runs from the far side of the piece behind it to the near side of the piece ahead, square-cut both ends in plan.
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
Centre: a triangle 1.4 in across its inscribed circle is left. Fill it with a plug cut from one wedge laid flat, or leave it open as a vent.
fitting: The first piece meets the 45° slope with its bark: it touches along one line, and leaves a wedge-shaped gap above it -- caulk it or pack it.

prep.name: Stock: from log to wedges (1/8 log)

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
